Store sales floor furnished in parts/room-10.mjs: goods barrels with lanterns and potted poppies under the shop windows, stock chests on the side walls, door lane and back row kept clear. Built via make.sh with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE writes.
Room check: 22/22 cells lit (min 10, none dark), FIT OK. Walk is OK only with the entrance steps; those belong to Fittings, so the room reads UNREACHABLE in the real build until they land.
The room is sparse: a shelf of pots and candles on the west wall would read better as a shop, and I did not add one.
left: Walkability depends on the store entrance steps (Fittings part): spruce_stairs facing south at x 88..91, z 6, y 1. Without them `mcd room` says UNREACHABLE for all 22 floor cells. Verified OK in a scratch copy with those steps added.
Focal piece is thin: the west-wall stock shelf is two chests and barrels with lanterns. A shelf of trapdoors or slabs with pots and candles would read more like a company store; not added for time.
plan.md checklist has no room line, so nothing ticked there. elements.md item 32 is only partly covered: barrels and stock chests are here, the counter is in room 11.

waste.what: Checking walkability needed a scratch copy of build.nbt with the entrance steps added by hand, to see whether the room was really reachable.
waste.cost: one extra node script and a /tmp scratch build, about 2 minutes
waste.tool: `mcd room` could report which entrance cells are missing (the steps or door approach) and whether the room is reachable once the Fittings part lands, instead of only UNREACHABLE.

waste.what: The plan tool prints the floor as 'floor y=6' for a room whose floor is y 3, so the furniture layer had to be inferred from the grid.
waste.cost: a few minutes of reading output and guessing the floor layer
waste.tool: `mcd plan --rooms` should print the floor y it used and allow `--y` to pick the layer.

waste.what: Checked the room look by eye from one above-view render; the chests and barrels read as plain boxes, so judging whether the store reads as a shop was by eye.
waste.tool: a `mcd rooms` interior eye view for a room that is only 8 by 3 would help judge it from inside.

companions.task: build the store's entrance steps at x 88..91, z 6 (spruce_stairs facing south, y 1), which make the sales floor reachable from the street; I would have handed them this for the Fittings part.
the stock shelving: a wall of trapdoor shelves or slabs with flower pots and candles along the west wall, which would make the focal piece read as a company store.
